case_objective: Produce a single 2D environment concept layout that re-derives the spatial composition, layered depth, form language and restrained palette observed in the supplied landscape concept panel, using the supplied character sheet to establish figure-to-environment scale, so a downstream environment art team can read the intended look and depth organization of a snow-and-ridge biome.
case_title: Reference-led 2D environment concept layout for an alpine endless-runner biome

deliverables.description: One 2D environment concept layout for the opening high-ridge biome, re-deriving from the supplied reference panels the spatial composition, layered depth, form language and restrained palette, with a rider-scale figure relationship established from the supplied character sheet. Delivered as a single landscape image or PDF page at approximately the references' aspect; no embedded annotation or provenance text is required.

inputs.instruction: New internal commission (hypothetical, not a historical client brief): the studio is prototyping a 2D endless-runner level and needs one environment concept layout for the opening 'high ridge' biome. Subject: a side-scrolling alpine slope traversed left to right, with a rider-scale silhouette relationship and layered mountain depth. Visual intent: quiet, geometric, painterly-vector look; strong horizontal layering; clear separation of playable foreground band from atmospheric distance. Communicate the biome's spatial composition and mood, not a finished in-game asset.
inputs.rationale: The task prompt (i1) in the intent graph is a request describing concept, subject matter and visual intent. No historical client request was downloaded, so this is authored as a clearly hypothetical commission consistent with the real assets, without asserting any real client, affiliation or event.

inputs.instruction: Presentation preferences for the deliverable (hypothetical): a single landscape canvas at the same aspect as the supplied references (roughly 1334x750, i.e. approximately 16:9), delivered as one flattened raster image (PNG or JPG) or a PDF page at that aspect; no text annotations required on the image itself; the working file is not scored. Mock-up scale is 1:1 pixel at the stated canvas size for review on a standard monitor. These are presentation choices, not measured facts about any real scene.
inputs.rationale: i2 covers explicit layout dimensions and viewing conditions. No measured dimension record was supplied for a target scene, so this is framed as an authored presentation preference for a new deliverable rather than a claimed measurement.

The reference imagery requirement is met by two present, inspected, relevant raster panels from the same project: a six-panel landscape series establishing layered mountain depth, horizon arrangement and a restrained palette (file2 s3-s8; canvas geometry in s9), and a character sheet establishing figure proportions and scale relationships (file1 s1; canvas geometry in s2). These are references for the worker to interpret; the panel set inspires a new biome concept and is not required to depict the finished scene requested. Segment descriptions are model visual observations and remain unverified.

limitations: All segment descriptions for file1 and file2 are model visual observations (verification_status: model_observation_unverified); the panel subjects, palettes and spatial arrangements have not been independently proven and must be confirmed by a human before they are treated as fact.

The six landscape panel segments are separate crops of a single sheet; they do not establish that these are six sequential frames, a single continuous scene, or any temporal order. No continuity between panels should be assumed.

No measured dimensions, blueprint, or target-scene measurements were supplied; canvas size and aspect are grounded only in the two reference files' pixel dimensions (programmatic extraction, source_located) and in authored presentation preferences.

No historical client brief, brand guidelines, or style bible was downloaded; the commission scope and presentation choices at i1 and i2 are synthetic instructions authored for this case, not real records.

License status for both source files is 'unknown' with redistribution_allowed false; the deliverable must not reproduce the reference panels or imply affiliation with the original project or originator.
Whether a 2D layout or a 3D mock-up is more appropriate cannot be settled from the assets alone; that branch is the worker's professional judgment at i6, and only the chosen branch is scored.

The reference panels depict varied biomes (green ridge, snow peak, sunset, desert, pastel ridges, twilight); they do not themselves define the high-ridge biome requested, so the worker's re-derivation — not a copy — is the intended operation.

operations.description: Interpret the brief, the presentation preferences and the two reference panels together, judging which spatial and stylistic elements must carry into the new layout: layered ridge silhouettes, horizon placement, foreground-to-distance scale drop, the conifer and rock form language, and the restrained per-panel temperature shifts. Decide which panel(s) to draw on for the ridge biome and which stylistic directions to hold as the team's target.

Define the visual content the concept must convey: the focal traversable slope band, the playable foreground versus atmospheric far ridges, the presence and scale of a rider/character silhouette using the character-sheet proportions, the density of conifer and rock elements, and the level of detail appropriate to an early environment concept rather than a finished asset.

Decide, from the design stage, the content complexity and the stated preferences, whether the concept is best expressed as a 2D layout or a 3D mock-up; the underlying task permits either. Commit to one branch and justify the choice in terms of readability of layering and speed of iteration.

Derive the composition from the references: horizontal banding of ridge layers, left-to-right traversal path, perspective or elevation treatment for the side-scrolling view, scale relationships between foreground slope, mid ridges and far peaks, and the lighting and color treatment (sky-to-ground value steps) that communicate depth and mood.
